53	
54	    @classmethod
55	    def parse(cls, raw: Any) -> "Map":
56	        if not isinstance(raw, dict):
57	            raise ValidationError("map must be an object")
58	        allowed = {"id", "width", "height", "grid", "obstacle"}
59	        unknown = sorted(set(raw) - allowed)
60	        if unknown:
61	            raise ValidationError(f"map contains unknown fields: {', '.join(unknown)}")
62	        required = {"id", "width", "height", "grid"}
63	        missing = sorted(required - set(raw))
64	        if missing:
65	            raise ValidationError(f"map is missing required fields: {', '.join(missing)}")
66	        map_id = identifier(raw["id"], "map id")
67	        width = integer(raw["width"], "width", 1, MAX_DIMENSION)
68	        height = integer(raw["height"], "height", 1, MAX_DIMENSION)
69	        if width * height > MAX_CELLS:
70	            raise ValidationError(f"map may not exceed {MAX_CELLS} cells")
71	        if "grid" in raw and isinstance(raw["grid"], list) and len(raw["grid"]) != height:
72	            raise ValidationError(f"grid must be an array of exactly {height} row strings")
73	        obstacle = raw.get("obstacle", "#")
74	        if not isinstance(obstacle, str) or len(obstacle) != 1 or obstacle.isspace():
75	            raise ValidationError("obstacle must be a single non-whitespace character")
76	        grid = raw["grid"]
77	        if not isinstance(grid, list) or len(grid) != height:
78	            raise ValidationError(f"grid must be an array of exactly {height} row strings")
79	        rows: list[str] = []
80	        for index, row in enumerate(grid):
81	            if not isinstance(row, str):
82	                raise ValidationError(f"grid row {index} must be a string")
83	            if len(row) != width:
84	                raise ValidationError(f"grid row {index} must be exactly {width} characters long")
85	            for column, char in enumerate(row):
86	                if char not in (".", obstacle):
87	                    raise ValidationError(
88	                        f"grid row {index} column {column} must be '.' or the obstacle character {obstacle!r}"
89	                    )
90	            rows.append(row)
91	        return cls(map_id, width, height, tuple(rows), obstacle)
92	
93	    def walkable(self, cell: Point) -> bool:
94	        x, y = cell
95	        if x < 0 or y < 0 or x >= self.width or y >= self.height:
96	            return False
97	        return self.rows[y][x] != self.obstacle
98	
99	    def index(self, cell: Point) -> int:
100	        return cell[1] * self.width + cell[0]
101	
102	    def neighbors(self, cell: Point) -> tuple[Point, ...]:
103	        x, y = cell
104	        candidates = ((x + 1, y), (x, y + 1), (x - 1, y), (x, y - 1))
105	        return tuple(candidate for candidate in candidates if self.walkable(candidate))
106	
107	    def as_dict(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
108	        return {
109	            "id": self.id,
110	            "width": self.width,
111	            "height": self.height,
112	            "grid": list(self.rows),
113	            "obstacle": self.obstacle,
114	        }
115	
116	
117	@dataclass(frozen=True)
118	class Agent:
119	    id: str
120	    start: Point
121	    goal: Point
122	
123	    @classmethod
124	    def parse(cls, raw: Any, map_record: Map, field: str) -> "Agent":
125	        if not isinstance(raw, dict):
126	            raise ValidationError(f"{field} must be an object")
127	        unknown = sorted(set(raw) - {"id", "start", "goal"})
128	        if unknown:
129	            raise ValidationError(f"{field} contains unknown fields: {', '.join(unknown)}")
130	        missing = sorted({"id", "start", "goal"} - set(raw))
131	        if missing:
132	            raise ValidationError(f"{field} is missing required fields: {', '.join(missing)}")
133	        agent_id = identifier(raw["id"], f"{field}.id")
134	        start = point(raw["start"], f"{field}.start", map_record.width, map_record.height)
135	        goal = point(raw["goal"], f"{field}.goal", map_record.width, map_record.height)
136	        if not map_record.walkable(start):
137	            raise ValidationError(f"{field}.start {list(start)} is an obstacle cell")
138	        if not map_record.walkable(goal):
139	            raise ValidationError(f"{field}.goal {list(goal)} is an obstacle cell")
140	        return cls(agent_id, start, goal)
141	
142	    def as_dict(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
143	        return {"id": self.id, "start": list(self.start), "goal": list(self.goal)}
144	
145	
146	@dataclass(frozen=True)
147	class Mission:
148	    id: str
149	    map_id: str
150	    agents: tuple[Agent, ...]
151	
152	    @classmethod
153	    def parse(cls, raw: Any, map_record: Map) -> "Mission":
154	        if not isinstance(raw, dict):
155	            raise ValidationError("mission must be an object")
156	        unknown = sorted(set(raw) - {"id", "map_id", "agents"})
157	        if unknown:
158	            raise ValidationError(f"mission contains unknown fields: {', '.join(unknown)}")
159	        missing = sorted({"id", "map_id", "agents"} - set(raw))
160	        if missing:
161	            raise ValidationError(f"mission is missing required fields: {', '.join(missing)}")
162	        mission_id = identifier(raw["id"], "mission id")
163	        map_id = identifier(raw["map_id"], "map_id")
164	        raw_agents = raw["agents"]
165	        if not isinstance(raw_agents, list) or not raw_agents:
166	            raise ValidationError("agents must be a non-empty array")
167	        if len(raw_agents) > MAX_AGENTS:
168	            raise ValidationError(f"a mission may not exceed {MAX_AGENTS} agents")
169	        agents = tuple(
170	            Agent.parse(entry, map_record, f"agents[{index}]") for index, entry in enumerate(raw_agents)
171	        )
172	        ids = [agent.id for agent in agents]
173	        if len(set(ids)) != len(ids):
174	            raise ValidationError("agent ids must be unique within a mission")
175	        starts = [agent.start for agent in agents]
176	        if len(set(starts)) != len(starts):
177	            raise ValidationError("agent start cells must be unique: two agents may not start on one cell")
178	        for agent in agents:
179	            if agent.start == agent.goal:
180	                raise ValidationError(f"agent {agent.id} already starts on its goal cell")
181	        return cls(mission_id, map_id, agents)
182	
183	    def order(self, priority: list[str]) -> tuple[Agent, ...]:
184	        by_id = {agent.id: agent for agent in self.agents}
185	        return tuple(by_id[agent_id] for agent_id in priority)
186	
187	    def as_dict(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
188	        return {"id": self.id, "map_id": self.map_id, "agents": [agent.as_dict() for agent in self.agents]}

1	"""Space-time A* planning for a single agent plus joint resolution for a mission.
2	
3	The public contract of this module is intentionally small:
4	
5	* :func:`distance_map` -- static BFS distances to a goal, ignoring other agents.
6	* :func:`space_time_astar` -- one-agent search in a time-expanded grid.
7	* :func:`detect_conflicts` -- vertex and edge-swap conflicts in a finished plan.
8	* :func:`plan_mission` -- joint planning for a mission.
9	
10	Joint planning has two stages, in this order:
11	
12	1. **Prioritized planning.** Agents are planned in priority order; each low-level
13	   search treats the paths of all higher-priority agents as moving obstacles.
14	   When an order fails, the next order in a deterministic permutation sequence is
15	   tried. This is cheap and resolves the common cases.
16	2. **Constraint tree.** If no priority order succeeds, a conflict-tree search
17	   (the outer loop of conflict-based search) branches on a concrete conflict:
18	   one child forbids one agent the conflicted cell or edge at that timestep. The
19	   tree is best-first by total cost, so it never misses a plan that an
20	   intermediate priority order hid behind a bad first choice. It is bounded by
21	   `tree_budget` nodes.
22	
23	A mission is reported `unsolvable` only when the priority orders are exhausted
24	**and** the constraint tree is either fully explored without a solution or hits
25	its node budget. No path data is ever fabricated.
26	
27	Determinism: every ordering, tie-break, and list in this module derives from
28	sorted agent identifiers, so the same map and mission always yield one plan.
29	"""
30	
31	from __future__ import annotations
32	
33	import heapq
34	from dataclasses import dataclass
35	from itertools import permutations
36	from typing import Iterable
37	
38	from .model import Agent, Mission, Point
39	
40	Move = tuple[int, int]
41	Path = tuple[Point, ...]
42	ConstraintSet = dict[str, tuple[frozenset[tuple[Point, int]], frozenset[tuple[Point, int, Point]]]]
43	
44	DEFAULT_ORDER_BUDGET = 24
45	DEFAULT_TREE_BUDGET = 64
46	DEFAULT_HOLD_BUDGET = 12
47	MAX_EXPANSIONS = 200_000
48	# A schedule never needs more ticks than this: every low-level search runs with
49	# this as its horizon, and the planner only ever asks for paths that start from
50	# the mission's own start cells, so the bound also caps how long an impossible
51	# mission is searched before the verdict is unsolvable.
52	MAX_TIMESTEP = 40
53	
54	# Expansion order is fixed and deterministic -- wait first, then the four moves;
55	# ties in the A* heap fall back to the insertion counter, so no set/dict
56	# iteration order can leak into a plan.
57	DIRECTIONS: tuple[Move, ...] = ((0, 0), (1, 0), (0, 1), (-1, 0), (0, -1))
58	
59	
60	@dataclass(frozen=True)
61	class Conflict:
62	    """A collision between two agents, or an impossible single-agent goal."""
63	
64	    type: str
65	    timestep: int
66	    agent: str
67	    other: str | None
68	    position: Point
69	    other_position: Point | None
70	    message: str
71	
72	    def as_dict(self) -> dict:
73	        return {
74	            "type": self.type,
75	            "timestep": self.timestep,
76	            "agent": self.agent,
77	            "other": self.other,
78	            "position": list(self.position),
79	            "other_position": list(self.other_position) if self.other_position is not None else None,
80	            "message": self.message,
81	        }
82	
83	    def as_key(self) -> tuple:
84	        return (
85	            self.type,
86	            self.timestep,
87	            self.agent,
88	            self.other or "",
89	            self.position,
90	            self.other_position,
91	        )
92	
93	
94	# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
95	# static geometry
96	# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
97	
98	
99	def distance_map(map_record, goal: Point) -> list[int | None]:
100	    """Breadth-first move distances from every cell to `goal` on the static grid.
101	
102	    Obstacle cells and cells that cannot reach `goal` are `None`. Other agents
103	    are ignored, which makes this a valid (admissible) lower bound.
104	    """
105	    distances: list[int | None] = [None] * (map_record.width * map_record.height)
106	    if not map_record.walkable(goal):
107	        return distances
108	    distances[map_record.index(goal)] = 0
109	    frontier = [goal]
110	    while frontier:
111	        following: list[Point] = []
112	        for cell in frontier:
113	            next_distance = distances[map_record.index(cell)] + 1  # type: ignore[operator]
114	            for neighbor in map_record.neighbors(cell):
115	                index = map_record.index(neighbor)
116	                if distances[index] is None:
117	                    distances[index] = next_distance
118	                    following.append(neighbor)
119	        frontier = following
120	    return distances
121	
122	
123	def _heuristic(cell: Point, goal: Point) -> int:
124	    return abs(cell[0] - goal[0]) + abs(cell[1] - goal[1])
125	
126	
127	# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
128	# single-agent space-time A*
129	# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
130	
131	
132	def position_at(path: Path, timestep: int) -> Point | None:
133	    """Cell occupied at `timestep`, or `None` once the agent has finished.
134	
135	    An agent's plan ends on its goal: it is done after `len(path) - 1` ticks, so
136	    it occupies no cell for every later timestep. A finished agent therefore
137	    never conflicts with an agent that still runs, and two agents can never
138	    settle on one cell.
139	    """
140	    if 0 <= timestep < len(path):
141	        return path[timestep]
142	    return None
143	
144	
145	def space_time_astar(
146	    map_record,
147	    agent: Agent,
148	    planned: list[tuple[str, Path]] | None = None,
149	    distance_to_goal: list[int | None] | None = None,
150	    forbidden_cells: frozenset[tuple[Point, int]] = frozenset(),
151	    forbidden_edges: frozenset[tuple[Point, int, Point]] = frozenset(),
152	    hold: int = 0,
153	) -> tuple[Path | None, Conflict | None]:
154	    """Plan `agent` in space and time.
155	
156	    The returned path is time indexed: `path[t]` is the cell the agent occupies
157	    at timestep `t`, so it stays contiguous and ends on the goal. A plan may
158	    include waits, and once the agent has finished it reads as `None` from
159	    :func:`position_at`, so a finished agent blocks nothing.
160	
161	    `hold` makes the agent stay on its start cell for that many ticks before it
162	    may move anywhere else. The joint planner uses it to explore "let the other
163	    agent go first" without forbidding the start cell outright.
164	
165	    Pruned during expansion:
166	
167	    * `planned` -- paths of higher-priority agents;
168	    * `forbidden_cells` -- `(cell, timestep)` the agent may not occupy;
169	    * `forbidden_edges` -- `(from_cell, timestep, to_cell)` the agent may not
170	      traverse; both directions of a traded edge are forbidden together.
171	
172	    Returns `(path, None)` on success, or `(None, conflict)` naming the blocking
173	    constraint when the goal cannot be reached under them.
174	    """
175	    planned = planned or []
176	    if distance_to_goal is None:
177	        distance_to_goal = distance_map(map_record, agent.goal)
178	    index_of_start = map_record.index(agent.start)
179	    if distance_to_goal[index_of_start] is None:
180	        return None, Conflict(
181	            "unreachable_goal",
182	            0,
183	            agent.id,
184	            None,
185	            agent.start,
186	            None,
187	            f"agent {agent.id} cannot reach its goal from {list(agent.start)} on the static grid",
188	        )
189	
190	    def occupant(cell: Point, timestep: int, came_from: Point) -> tuple[str, Point] | None:
191	        """A higher-priority agent that makes this move a vertex conflict or a swap.
192	
193	        Occupancy is read with :func:`position_at`, so a higher-priority agent
194	        blocks exactly the cells it holds on exactly the ticks it holds them --
195	        it stops blocking once it finishes on its goal. Following is legal:
196	        entering a cell that another agent leaves on the same tick never puts two
197	        agents on one cell.
198	        """
199	        for other_id, path in planned:
200	            if position_at(path, timestep) == cell:
201	                return (other_id, cell)
202	            if position_at(path, timestep - 1) == cell and position_at(path, timestep) == came_from:
203	                # The other agent moves from `cell` into `came_from` on this very
204	                # tick, so this move would trade the two agents' cells.
205	                return (other_id, cell)
206	        return None
207	
208	    start = agent.start
209	    counter = 0
210	    # States are (cell, timestep) pairs: with time-indexed constraints a cell may
211	    # be usable at one timestep and blocked at another, so arrival time is part of
212	    # the state. The heap is ordered by estimated total cost, and `came_from` is
213	    # keyed by state so a wait and a move into the same cell stay distinct.
214	    heap: list[tuple[int, int, int, Point]] = [(distance_to_goal[index_of_start], 0, counter, start)]
215	    came_from: dict[tuple[Point, int], tuple[Point, int] | None] = {(start, 0): None}
216	    reached: set[tuple[Point, int]] = {(start, 0)}
217	    expansions = 0
218	
219	    while heap:
220	        _, timestep, _, cell = heapq.heappop(heap)
221	        if timestep > MAX_TIMESTEP:
222	            continue
223	        expansions += 1
224	        if expansions > MAX_EXPANSIONS:
225	            break
226	        if cell == agent.goal and (cell, timestep) not in forbidden_cells:
227	            return _fill_waits(came_from, (cell, timestep), agent.goal), None
228	
229	        following = timestep + 1
230	        for move in DIRECTIONS:
231	            neighbor = (cell[0] + move[0], cell[1] + move[1])
232	            if not map_record.walkable(neighbor):
233	                continue
234	            if timestep < hold and neighbor != start:
235	                continue
236	            if (neighbor, following) in forbidden_cells:
237	                continue
238	            if (cell, following, neighbor) in forbidden_edges:
239	                continue
240	            if (neighbor, following) in reached:
241	                continue
242	            if occupant(neighbor, following, cell) is not None:
243	                continue
244	            reached.add((neighbor, following))
245	            came_from[(neighbor, following)] = (cell, timestep)
246	            counter += 1
247	            heapq.heappush(
248	                heap,
249	                (distance_to_goal[map_record.index(neighbor)] + following, following, counter, neighbor),
250	            )
251	
252	    return None, _exhausted(agent, planned, forbidden_cells, forbidden_edges)
253	
254	
255	def _exhausted(
256	    agent: Agent,
257	    planned: list[tuple[str, Path]],
258	    forbidden_cells: frozenset[tuple[Point, int]],
259	    forbidden_edges: frozenset[tuple[Point, int, Point]],
260	) -> Conflict:
261	    """Explain an exhausted search; the usual causes are checked in order."""
262	    for other_id, path in planned:
263	        if path[-1] == agent.goal:
264	            return Conflict(
265	                "vertex",
266	                0,
267	                agent.id,
268	                other_id,
269	                agent.goal,
270	                agent.goal,
271	                f"agent {agent.id} cannot reach goal {list(agent.goal)}: it is also the goal of "
272	                f"{other_id}, whose plan occupies the route",
273	            )
274	    if forbidden_cells:
275	        timestep, cell = min((step, position) for position, step in forbidden_cells)
276	        return Conflict(
277	            "vertex",
278	            timestep,
279	            agent.id,
280	            None,
281	            cell,
282	            None,
283	            f"agent {agent.id} cannot reach goal {list(agent.goal)}: {list(cell)} is forbidden "
284	            f"at t={timestep}",
285	        )
286	    if forbidden_edges:
287	        timestep, edge = min((step, (source, target)) for source, step, target in forbidden_edges)
288	        return Conflict(
289	            "edge",
290	            timestep,
291	            agent.id,
292	            None,
293	            edge[0],
294	            edge[1],
295	            f"agent {agent.id} cannot reach goal {list(agent.goal)}: the edge "
296	            f"{list(edge[0])}->{list(edge[1])} is forbidden at t={timestep}",
297	        )
298	    return Conflict(
299	        "unreachable_goal",
300	        0,
301	        agent.id,
302	        None,
303	        agent.goal,
304	        None,
305	        f"agent {agent.id} has no conflict-free route to goal {list(agent.goal)} under these constraints",
306	    )
307	
308	
309	def _fill_waits(
310	    came_from: dict[tuple[Point, int], tuple[Point, int] | None],
311	    current: tuple[Point, int],
312	    goal: Point,
313	) -> Path:
314	    """Rebuild the time-indexed path from the goal state back to the start."""
315	    cells: list[Point] = []
316	    node: tuple[Point, int] | None = current
317	    while node is not None:
318	        cells.append(node[0])
319	        node = came_from[node]
320	    cells.reverse()
321	    assert cells[-1] == goal
322	    return tuple(cells)
323	
324	
325	# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
326	# joint plan validation
327	# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
328	
329	
330	def detect_conflicts(order: tuple[Agent, ...], paths: list[Path]) -> list[Conflict]:
331	    """Every vertex conflict and edge swap in a joint plan, ordered by timestep."""
332	    found: list[Conflict] = []
333	    horizon = max((len(path) for path in paths), default=0)
334	    for timestep in range(horizon):
335	        for left in range(len(order)):
336	            first = position_at(paths[left], timestep)
337	            if first is None:
338	                continue
339	            for right in range(left + 1, len(order)):
340	                second = position_at(paths[right], timestep)
341	                if second is None:
342	                    continue
343	                if first == second:
344	                    found.append(
345	                        Conflict(
346	                            "vertex",
347	                            timestep,
348	                            order[left].id,
349	                            order[right].id,
350	                            first,
351	                            second,
352	                            f"{order[left].id} and {order[right].id} both occupy {list(first)} at t={timestep}",
353	                        )
354	                    )
355	                    continue
356	                if timestep + 1 >= horizon:
357	                    continue
358	                left_next = position_at(paths[left], timestep + 1)
359	                right_next = position_at(paths[right], timestep + 1)
360	                if left_next is None or right_next is None:
361	                    continue
362	                if left_next == second and right_next == first:
363	                    found.append(
364	                        Conflict(
365	                            "edge",
366	                            timestep,
367	                            order[left].id,
368	                            order[right].id,
369	                            first,
370	                            second,
371	                            f"{order[left].id} and {order[right].id} swap {list(first)} and "
372	                            f"{list(second)} at t={timestep}",
373	                        )
374	                    )
375	    return sorted(found, key=lambda conflict: conflict.as_key())
376	
377	
378	def makespan(paths: Iterable[Path]) -> int:
379	    return max((len(path) - 1 for path in paths), default=0)
380	
381	
382	# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
383	# joint planning
384	# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
385	
386	
387	@dataclass(frozen=True)
388	class PlanResult:
389	    """`method` is `priority` or `constraint_tree`; `order` drives the agent listing."""
390	
391	    status: str
392	    method: str
393	    order: tuple[str, ...]
394	    paths: tuple[Path, ...]
395	    conflicts: tuple[Conflict, ...]
396	    orders_tried: int
397	    orders_budget: int
398	
399	    @property
400	    def solution_makespan(self) -> int:
401	        return makespan(self.paths)
402	
403	
404	def plan_mission(
405	    map_record,
406	    mission: Mission,
407	    requested_priority: list[str] | None = None,
408	    order_budget: int = DEFAULT_ORDER_BUDGET,
409	    tree_budget: int = DEFAULT_TREE_BUDGET,
410	) -> PlanResult:
411	    """Resolve `mission` with prioritized planning, then a constraint tree.
412	
413	    `map_record` is duck-typed: it needs `width`, `height`, `walkable`, `index`,
414	    and `neighbors` (that is, :class:`swarmgrid.model.Map`).
415	    """
416	    agents = tuple(sorted(mission.agents, key=lambda agent: agent.id))
417	    distance_from_goal: dict[Point, list[int | None]] = {
418	        agent.goal: distance_map(map_record, agent.goal) for agent in agents
419	    }
420	    unreachable = [
421	        Conflict(
422	            "unreachable_goal",
423	            0,
424	            agent.id,
425	            None,
426	            agent.goal,
427	            None,
428	            f"agent {agent.id} goal {list(agent.goal)} is unreachable on the static map",
429	        )
430	        for agent in agents
431	        if distance_from_goal[agent.goal][map_record.index(agent.start)] is None
432	    ]
433	    if unreachable:
434	        return PlanResult(
435	            status="unsolvable",
436	            method="none",
437	            order=(),
438	            paths=(),
439	            conflicts=tuple(sorted(unreachable, key=lambda conflict: conflict.as_key())),
440	            orders_tried=0,
441	            orders_budget=_orders_budget(len(agents), order_budget, requested_priority),
442	        )
443	
444	    budget = _orders_budget(len(agents), order_budget, requested_priority)
445	    if requested_priority is not None:
446	        sequence: list[tuple[str, ...]] = [tuple(requested_priority)]
447	    else:
448	        sequence = _order_sequence(tuple(agent.id for agent in agents), budget)
449	
450	    conflicts: list[Conflict] = []
451	    tried = 0
452	    for order_ids in sequence:
453	        tried += 1
454	        order = tuple(next(agent for agent in agents if agent.id == agent_id) for agent_id in order_ids)
455	        paths, failure = _run_order(map_record, order, distance_from_goal)
456	        if paths is None:
457	            if failure is not None:
458	                conflicts.append(failure)
459	            continue
460	        joint = detect_conflicts(order, paths)
461	        if joint:
462	            conflicts.extend(joint)
463	            continue
464	        return PlanResult(
465	            status="solved",
466	            method="priority",
467	            order=order_ids,
468	            paths=tuple(paths),
469	            conflicts=(),
470	            orders_tried=tried,
471	            orders_budget=budget,
472	        )
473	
474	    if requested_priority is None:
475	        solution = _constraint_tree(map_record, agents, distance_from_goal, tree_budget, budget)
476	        if solution is not None:
477	            paths, tree_conflicts = solution
478	            if not tree_conflicts:
479	                return PlanResult(
480	                    status="solved",
481	                    method="constraint_tree",
482	                    order=tuple(agent.id for agent in agents),
483	                    paths=tuple(paths),
484	                    conflicts=(),
485	                    orders_tried=tried,
486	                    orders_budget=budget,
487	                )
488	            conflicts.extend(tree_conflicts)
489	
490	    return PlanResult(
491	        status="unsolvable",
492	        method="none",
493	        order=(),
494	        paths=(),
495	        conflicts=tuple(_deduplicate(conflicts)),
496	        orders_tried=tried,
497	        orders_budget=budget,
498	    )
499	
500	
501	def _run_order(
502	    map_record,
503	    order: tuple[Agent, ...],
504	    distance_from_goal: dict[Point, list[int | None]],
505	    constraints: ConstraintSet | None = None,
506	    first_hold: int = 0,
507	) -> tuple[list[Path] | None, Conflict | None]:
508	    """Plan `order` one agent at a time, each treating the earlier paths as moving obstacles.
509	
510	    Waiting is a legal move, but a step planner enters the grid as early as it
511	    can, so on a bottleneck it can walk into a pocket. Every agent is therefore
512	    offered a head start: it may hold its start cell for a few ticks before it
513	    enters the grid, and `first_hold` does the same for the highest-priority
514	    agent, whose early entrance can be what blocks everybody else. The first
515	    option that actually routes the agent is used.
516	    """
517	    constraints = constraints or {}
518	    planned: list[tuple[str, Path]] = []
519	    for index, agent in enumerate(order):
520	        cells, edges = constraints.get(agent.id, (frozenset(), frozenset()))
521	        if index == 0 and first_hold > 0:
522	            path, failure = space_time_astar(
523	                map_record,
524	                agent,
525	                planned,
526	                distance_from_goal[agent.goal],
527	                cells,
528	                edges,
529	                first_hold,
530	            )
531	            if path is None:
532	                assert failure is not None
533	                return None, failure
534	        else:
535	            path, failure = _route_with_wait(
536	                map_record, agent, planned, distance_from_goal, cells, edges
537	            )
538	            if path is None:
539	                assert failure is not None
540	                return None, failure
541	        planned.append((agent.id, path))
542	    return [path for _, path in planned], None
543	
544	
545	def _route_with_wait(
546	    map_record,
547	    agent: Agent,
548	    planned: list[tuple[str, Path]],
549	    distance_from_goal: dict[Point, list[int | None]],
550	    cells: frozenset[tuple[Point, int]],
551	    edges: frozenset[tuple[Point, int, Point]],
552	) -> tuple[Path | None, Conflict | None]:
553	    """Try routing `agent` after holding its start cell for 0..N ticks.
554	
555	    When every option fails, a two-agent goal contention is reported as a vertex
556	    conflict on the shared goal: that is the concrete cause, and it is far more
557	    useful to a caller than the bare "no route" dead end.
558	    """
559	    failure: Conflict | None = None
560	    for hold in range(DEFAULT_HOLD_BUDGET + 1):
561	        path, conflict = space_time_astar(
562	            map_record, agent, planned, distance_from_goal[agent.goal], cells, edges, hold
563	        )
564	        if path is not None:
565	            return path, None
566	        if failure is None:
567	            failure = conflict
568	    assert failure is not None
569	    for other_id, path in planned:
570	        if path[-1] == agent.goal:
571	            return None, Conflict(
572	                "vertex",
573	                0,
574	                agent.id,
575	                other_id,
576	                agent.goal,
577	                agent.goal,
578	                f"agent {agent.id} cannot reach goal {list(agent.goal)}: {other_id} is "
579	                f"planned to end there",
580	            )
581	    for other_id, path in planned:
582	        if path[-1] == agent.start:
583	            return None, Conflict(
584	                "vertex",
585	                len(path) - 1,
586	                agent.id,
587	                other_id,
588	                agent.start,
589	                agent.goal,
590	                f"agent {agent.id} is trapped on {list(agent.start)}: {other_id} finishes "
591	                f"there at t={len(path) - 1}",
592	            )
593	    return None, failure
594	
595	
596	def _order_sequence(default_order: tuple[str, ...], budget: int) -> list[tuple[str, ...]]:
597	    """The deterministic priority orders to try: the default first, then permutations."""
598	    budget = max(1, budget)
599	    ordered: list[tuple[str, ...]] = [default_order]
600	    for permutation in sorted(permutations(default_order)):
601	        if len(ordered) >= budget:
602	            break
603	        if permutation != default_order:
604	            ordered.append(permutation)
605	    return ordered
606	
607	
608	# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
609	# stage two: conflict tree (outer loop of conflict-based search)
610	# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
611	
612	
613	def _constraint_tree(
614	    map_record,
615	    agents: tuple[Agent, ...],
616	    distance_from_goal: dict[Point, list[int | None]],
617	    tree_budget: int,
618	    order_budget: int = DEFAULT_ORDER_BUDGET,
619	) -> tuple[list[Path], list[Conflict]] | None:
620	    """Best-first search over sets of per-agent space-time constraints.
621	
622	    Returns `(paths, [])` for a conflict-free joint plan. When no plan is found it
623	    returns `(infeasible_paths, [conflict])` explaining why: the failure blocking
624	    the best node when the tree ran out of budget, or an empty conflict list when
625	    every node it reached was infeasible and nothing was left to branch on.
626	    """
627	    root: ConstraintSet = {}
628	    paths, failure = _plan_all(map_record, agents, distance_from_goal, root, order_budget)
629	    if failure is None:
630	        return paths, []
631	    counter = 0
632	    heap: list[tuple[int, int, tuple]] = [
633	        (
634	            _paths_cost(paths) if len(paths) == len(agents) else INFEASIBLE_COST,
635	            counter,
636	            (root, paths, failure),
637	        )
638	    ]
639	    expanded = 0
640	
641	    while heap:
642	        _, _, (constraints, paths, failure) = heapq.heappop(heap)
643	        if failure is None:
644	            return paths, []
645	        if expanded >= tree_budget:
646	            return paths, [failure]
647	        expanded += 1
648	        for child in _branch(constraints, failure):
649	            child_paths, child_failure = _plan_all(
650	                map_record, agents, distance_from_goal, child, order_budget
651	            )
652	            counter += 1
653	            heapq.heappush(
654	                heap,
655	                (
656	                    _paths_cost(child_paths) if child_failure is None else INFEASIBLE_COST,
657	                    counter,
658	                    (child, child_paths, child_failure),
659	                ),
660	            )
661	    return paths, [failure]
662	
663	
664	INFEASIBLE_COST = 1 << 40
665	
666	
667	def _plan_all(
668	    map_record,
669	    agents: tuple[Agent, ...],
670	    distance_from_goal: dict[Point, list[int | None]],
671	    constraints: ConstraintSet,
672	    order_budget: int = DEFAULT_ORDER_BUDGET,
673	) -> tuple[list[Path], Conflict | None]:
674	    """Plan all agents at one node of the constraint tree.
675	
676	    Because a node's leaf planner plans one agent at a time, which agent yields is
677	    a real choice: on a bottleneck one order finds a plan and the reverse order
678	    traps the lower-priority agent. Every node therefore tries the deterministic
679	    priority orders and keeps a conflict-free plan if one appears. When none does,
680	    the node reports its blocking conflict so the tree can branch on it.
681	    """
682	    fallback: Conflict | None = None
683	    report: list[Path] | None = None
684	    for order_ids in _order_sequence(tuple(agent.id for agent in agents), order_budget):
685	        order = tuple(next(agent for agent in agents if agent.id == agent_id) for agent_id in order_ids)
686	        for first_hold in range(DEFAULT_HOLD_BUDGET + 1):
687	            outcome, failure = _run_order(
688	                map_record, order, distance_from_goal, constraints, first_hold
689	            )
690	            if outcome is not None:
691	                joint = detect_conflicts(order, outcome)
692	                if not joint:
693	                    ordered = {agent.id: path for agent, path in zip(order, outcome)}
694	                    return [ordered[agent.id] for agent in agents], None
695	                if report is None:
696	                    ordered = {agent.id: path for agent, path in zip(order, outcome)}
697	                    report = [ordered[agent.id] for agent in agents]
698	                conflict = joint[0]
699	            else:
700	                assert failure is not None
701	                conflict = failure
702	            if fallback is None:
703	                fallback = conflict
704	    # A plan that is complete but still conflicts names a concrete vertex or
705	    # swap, which is far more useful than the dead end of a single agent.
706	    if report is not None:
707	        conflicts = detect_conflicts(agents, report)
708	        if conflicts:
709	            return report, conflicts[0]
710	    return report or [], fallback
711	
712	
713	def _paths_cost(paths: list[Path]) -> int:
714	    return sum(len(path) - 1 for path in paths)
715	
716	
717	def _branch(constraints: ConstraintSet, conflict: Conflict) -> list[ConstraintSet]:
718	    """Children of a node: forbid the conflicted cell or edge to one of the agents.
719	
720	    A two-agent conflict branches on both agents, so the tree covers "the first
721	    agent yields" and "the second one does". A conflict that involves a single
722	    agent is branched on that agent, and a bare `unreachable_goal` cannot be
723	    branched on at all.
724	    """
725	    if conflict.other is None:
726	        if conflict.type == "unreachable_goal":
727	            return []
728	        pairs = [(conflict.agent, True)]
729	    else:
730	        pairs = [
731	            (conflict.agent if conflict.agent < conflict.other else conflict.other, False),
732	            (conflict.other if conflict.agent < conflict.other else conflict.agent, False),
733	        ]
734	    children: list[ConstraintSet] = []
735	    for agent_id, single_agent in pairs:
736	        child = {key: (set(cells), set(edges)) for key, (cells, edges) in constraints.items()}
737	        cells, edges = child.setdefault(agent_id, (set(), set()))
738	        if single_agent:
739	            if conflict.timestep == 0:
740	                continue
741	            edges.add((conflict.position, conflict.timestep - 1, conflict.position))
742	        elif conflict.type == "vertex":
743	            cells.add((conflict.position, conflict.timestep))
744	        else:
745	            other_position = conflict.other_position or conflict.position
746	            edges.add((conflict.position, conflict.timestep, other_position))
747	            edges.add((other_position, conflict.timestep, conflict.position))
748	        children.append(
749	            {key: (frozenset(value[0]), frozenset(value[1])) for key, value in sorted(child.items())}
750	        )
751	    return children
752	
753	
754	def _deduplicate(conflicts: list[Conflict]) -> list[Conflict]:
755	    seen: dict[tuple, Conflict] = {}
756	    for conflict in conflicts:
757	        seen.setdefault(conflict.as_key(), conflict)
758	    return sorted(seen.values(), key=lambda conflict: conflict.as_key())
759	
760	
761	def _orders_budget(agent_count: int, budget: int, requested: list[str] | None) -> int:
762	    if requested is not None:
763	        return 1
764	    if agent_count <= 1:
765	        return 1
766	    return max(1, min(budget, _factorial(agent_count)))
767	
768	
769	def _factorial(value: int) -> int:
770	    total = 1
771	    for factor in range(2, value + 1):
772	        total *= factor
773	    return total

"""Space-time A* planning for a single agent plus joint resolution for a mission.

The public contract of this module is intentionally small:

* :func:`distance_map` -- static BFS distances to a goal, ignoring other agents.
* :func:`space_time_astar` -- one-agent search in a time-expanded grid.
* :func:`detect_conflicts` -- vertex and edge-swap conflicts in a finished plan.
* :func:`plan_mission` -- joint planning for a mission.

Joint planning has two stages, in this order:

1. **Prioritized planning.** Agents are planned in priority order; each low-level
   search treats the paths of all higher-priority agents as moving obstacles.
   When an order fails, the next order in a deterministic permutation sequence is
   tried. This is cheap and resolves the common cases.
2. **Constraint tree.** If no priority order succeeds, a conflict-tree search
   (the outer loop of conflict-based search) branches on a concrete conflict:
   one child forbids one agent the conflicted cell or edge at that timestep. The
   tree is best-first by total cost, so it never misses a plan that an
   intermediate priority order hid behind a bad first choice. It is bounded by
   `tree_budget` nodes.

A mission is reported `unsolvable` only when the priority orders are exhausted
**and** the constraint tree is either fully explored without a solution or hits
its node budget. No path data is ever fabricated.

Determinism: every ordering, tie-break, and list in this module derives from
sorted agent identifiers, so the same map and mission always yield one plan.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import heapq
from dataclasses import dataclass
from itertools import permutations
from typing import Iterable

from .model import Agent, Mission, Point

Move = tuple[int, int]
Path = tuple[Point, ...]
ConstraintSet = dict[str, tuple[frozenset[tuple[Point, int]], frozenset[tuple[Point, int, Point]]]]

DEFAULT_ORDER_BUDGET = 24
DEFAULT_TREE_BUDGET = 64
DEFAULT_HOLD_BUDGET = 12
MAX_EXPANSIONS = 200_000
# A schedule never needs more ticks than this: every low-level search runs with
# this as its horizon, and the planner only ever asks for paths that start from
# the mission's own start cells, so the bound also caps how long an impossible
# mission is searched before the verdict is unsolvable.
MAX_TIMESTEP = 40

# Expansion order is fixed and deterministic -- wait first, then the four moves;
# ties in the A* heap fall back to the insertion counter, so no set/dict
# iteration order can leak into a plan.
DIRECTIONS: tuple[Move, ...] = ((0, 0), (1, 0), (0, 1), (-1, 0), (0, -1))


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Conflict:
    """A collision between two agents, or an impossible single-agent goal."""

    type: str
    timestep: int
    agent: str
    other: str | None
    position: Point
    other_position: Point | None
    message: str

    def as_dict(self) -> dict:
        return {
            "type": self.type,
            "timestep": self.timestep,
            "agent": self.agent,
            "other": self.other,
            "position": list(self.position),
            "other_position": list(self.other_position) if self.other_position is not None else None,
            "message": self.message,
        }

    def as_key(self) -> tuple:
        return (
            self.type,
            self.timestep,
            self.agent,
            self.other or "",
            self.position,
            self.other_position,
        )


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# static geometry
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #


def distance_map(map_record, goal: Point) -> list[int | None]:
    """Breadth-first move distances from every cell to `goal` on the static grid.

    Obstacle cells and cells that cannot reach `goal` are `None`. Other agents
    are ignored, which makes this a valid (admissible) lower bound.
    """
    distances: list[int | None] = [None] * (map_record.width * map_record.height)
    if not map_record.walkable(goal):
        return distances
    distances[map_record.index(goal)] = 0
    frontier = [goal]
    while frontier:
        following: list[Point] = []
        for cell in frontier:
            next_distance = distances[map_record.index(cell)] + 1  # type: ignore[operator]
            for neighbor in map_record.neighbors(cell):
                index = map_record.index(neighbor)
                if distances[index] is None:
                    distances[index] = next_distance
                    following.append(neighbor)
        frontier = following
    return distances


def _heuristic(cell: Point, goal: Point) -> int:
    return abs(cell[0] - goal[0]) + abs(cell[1] - goal[1])


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# single-agent space-time A*
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #


def position_at(path: Path, timestep: int) -> Point | None:
    """Cell occupied at `timestep`, or `None` once the agent has finished.

    An agent's plan ends on its goal: it is done after `len(path) - 1` ticks, so
    it occupies no cell for every later timestep. A finished agent therefore
    never conflicts with an agent that still runs, and two agents can never
    settle on one cell.
    """
    if 0 <= timestep < len(path):
        return path[timestep]
    return None


def space_time_astar(
    map_record,
    agent: Agent,
    planned: list[tuple[str, Path]] | None = None,
    distance_to_goal: list[int | None] | None = None,
    forbidden_cells: frozenset[tuple[Point, int]] = frozenset(),
    forbidden_edges: frozenset[tuple[Point, int, Point]] = frozenset(),
    hold: int = 0,
) -> tuple[Path | None, Conflict | None]:
    """Plan `agent` in space and time.

    The returned path is time indexed: `path[t]` is the cell the agent occupies
    at timestep `t`, so it stays contiguous and ends on the goal. A plan may
    include waits, and once the agent has finished it reads as `None` from
    :func:`position_at`, so a finished agent blocks nothing.

    `hold` makes the agent stay on its start cell for that many ticks before it
    may move anywhere else. The joint planner uses it to explore "let the other
    agent go first" without forbidding the start cell outright.

    Pruned during expansion:

    * `planned` -- paths of higher-priority agents;
    * `forbidden_cells` -- `(cell, timestep)` the agent may not occupy;
    * `forbidden_edges` -- `(from_cell, timestep, to_cell)` the agent may not
      traverse; both directions of a traded edge are forbidden together.

    Returns `(path, None)` on success, or `(None, conflict)` naming the blocking
    constraint when the goal cannot be reached under them.
    """
    planned = planned or []
    if distance_to_goal is None:
        distance_to_goal = distance_map(map_record, agent.goal)
    index_of_start = map_record.index(agent.start)
    if distance_to_goal[index_of_start] is None:
        return None, Conflict(
            "unreachable_goal",
            0,
            agent.id,
            None,
            agent.start,
            None,
            f"agent {agent.id} cannot reach its goal from {list(agent.start)} on the static grid",
        )

    def occupant(cell: Point, timestep: int, came_from: Point) -> tuple[str, Point] | None:
        """A higher-priority agent that makes this move a vertex conflict or a swap.

        Occupancy is read with :func:`position_at`, so a higher-priority agent
        blocks exactly the cells it holds on exactly the ticks it holds them --
        it stops blocking once it finishes on its goal. Following is legal:
        entering a cell that another agent leaves on the same tick never puts two
        agents on one cell.
        """
        for other_id, path in planned:
            if position_at(path, timestep) == cell:
                return (other_id, cell)
            if position_at(path, timestep - 1) == cell and position_at(path, timestep) == came_from:
                # The other agent moves from `cell` into `came_from` on this very
                # tick, so this move would trade the two agents' cells.
                return (other_id, cell)
        return None

    start = agent.start
    counter = 0
    # States are (cell, timestep) pairs: with time-indexed constraints a cell may
    # be usable at one timestep and blocked at another, so arrival time is part of
    # the state. The heap is ordered by estimated total cost, and `came_from` is
    # keyed by state so a wait and a move into the same cell stay distinct.
    heap: list[tuple[int, int, int, Point]] = [(distance_to_goal[index_of_start], 0, counter, start)]
    came_from: dict[tuple[Point, int], tuple[Point, int] | None] = {(start, 0): None}
    reached: set[tuple[Point, int]] = {(start, 0)}
    expansions = 0

    while heap:
        _, timestep, _, cell = heapq.heappop(heap)
        if timestep > MAX_TIMESTEP:
            continue
        expansions += 1
        if expansions > MAX_EXPANSIONS:
            break
        if cell == agent.goal and (cell, timestep) not in forbidden_cells:
            return _fill_waits(came_from, (cell, timestep), agent.goal), None

        following = timestep + 1
        for move in DIRECTIONS:
            neighbor = (cell[0] + move[0], cell[1] + move[1])
            if not map_record.walkable(neighbor):
                continue
            if timestep < hold and neighbor != start:
                continue
            if (neighbor, following) in forbidden_cells:
                continue
            if (cell, following, neighbor) in forbidden_edges:
                continue
            if (neighbor, following) in reached:
                continue
            if occupant(neighbor, following, cell) is not None:
                continue
            reached.add((neighbor, following))
            came_from[(neighbor, following)] = (cell, timestep)
            counter += 1
            heapq.heappush(
                heap,
                (distance_to_goal[map_record.index(neighbor)] + following, following, counter, neighbor),
            )

    return None, _exhausted(agent, planned, forbidden_cells, forbidden_edges)


def _exhausted(
    agent: Agent,
    planned: list[tuple[str, Path]],
    forbidden_cells: frozenset[tuple[Point, int]],
    forbidden_edges: frozenset[tuple[Point, int, Point]],
) -> Conflict:
    """Explain an exhausted search; the usual causes are checked in order."""
    for other_id, path in planned:
        if path[-1] == agent.goal:
            return Conflict(
                "vertex",
                0,
                agent.id,
                other_id,
                agent.goal,
                agent.goal,
                f"agent {agent.id} cannot reach goal {list(agent.goal)}: it is also the goal of "
                f"{other_id}, whose plan occupies the route",
            )
    if forbidden_cells:
        timestep, cell = min((step, position) for position, step in forbidden_cells)
        return Conflict(
            "vertex",
            timestep,
            agent.id,
            None,
            cell,
            None,
            f"agent {agent.id} cannot reach goal {list(agent.goal)}: {list(cell)} is forbidden "
            f"at t={timestep}",
        )
    if forbidden_edges:
        timestep, edge = min((step, (source, target)) for source, step, target in forbidden_edges)
        return Conflict(
            "edge",
            timestep,
            agent.id,
            None,
            edge[0],
            edge[1],
            f"agent {agent.id} cannot reach goal {list(agent.goal)}: the edge "
            f"{list(edge[0])}->{list(edge[1])} is forbidden at t={timestep}",
        )
    return Conflict(
        "unreachable_goal",
        0,
        agent.id,
        None,
        agent.goal,
        None,
        f"agent {agent.id} has no conflict-free route to goal {list(agent.goal)} under these constraints",
    )


def _fill_waits(
    came_from: dict[tuple[Point, int], tuple[Point, int] | None],
    current: tuple[Point, int],
    goal: Point,
) -> Path:
    """Rebuild the time-indexed path from the goal state back to the start."""
    cells: list[Point] = []
    node: tuple[Point, int] | None = current
    while node is not None:
        cells.append(node[0])
        node = came_from[node]
    cells.reverse()
    assert cells[-1] == goal
    return tuple(cells)


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# joint plan validation
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #


def detect_conflicts(order: tuple[Agent, ...], paths: list[Path]) -> list[Conflict]:
    """Every vertex conflict and edge swap in a joint plan, ordered by timestep."""
    found: list[Conflict] = []
    horizon = max((len(path) for path in paths), default=0)
    for timestep in range(horizon):
        for left in range(len(order)):
            first = position_at(paths[left], timestep)
            if first is None:
                continue
            for right in range(left + 1, len(order)):
                second = position_at(paths[right], timestep)
                if second is None:
                    continue
                if first == second:
                    found.append(
                        Conflict(
                            "vertex",
                            timestep,
                            order[left].id,
                            order[right].id,
                            first,
                            second,
                            f"{order[left].id} and {order[right].id} both occupy {list(first)} at t={timestep}",
                        )
                    )
                    continue
                if timestep + 1 >= horizon:
                    continue
                left_next = position_at(paths[left], timestep + 1)
                right_next = position_at(paths[right], timestep + 1)
                if left_next is None or right_next is None:
                    continue
                if left_next == second and right_next == first:
                    found.append(
                        Conflict(
                            "edge",
                            timestep,
                            order[left].id,
                            order[right].id,
                            first,
                            second,
                            f"{order[left].id} and {order[right].id} swap {list(first)} and "
                            f"{list(second)} at t={timestep}",
                        )
                    )
    return sorted(found, key=lambda conflict: conflict.as_key())


def makespan(paths: Iterable[Path]) -> int:
    return max((len(path) - 1 for path in paths), default=0)


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# joint planning
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class PlanResult:
    """`method` is `priority` or `constraint_tree`; `order` drives the agent listing."""

    status: str
    method: str
    order: tuple[str, ...]
    paths: tuple[Path, ...]
    conflicts: tuple[Conflict, ...]
    orders_tried: int
    orders_budget: int

    @property
    def solution_makespan(self) -> int:
        return makespan(self.paths)


def plan_mission(
    map_record,
    mission: Mission,
    requested_priority: list[str] | None = None,
    order_budget: int = DEFAULT_ORDER_BUDGET,
    tree_budget: int = DEFAULT_TREE_BUDGET,
) -> PlanResult:
    """Resolve `mission` with prioritized planning, then a constraint tree.

    `map_record` is duck-typed: it needs `width`, `height`, `walkable`, `index`,
    and `neighbors` (that is, :class:`swarmgrid.model.Map`).
    """
    agents = tuple(sorted(mission.agents, key=lambda agent: agent.id))
    distance_from_goal: dict[Point, list[int | None]] = {
        agent.goal: distance_map(map_record, agent.goal) for agent in agents
    }
    unreachable = [
        Conflict(
            "unreachable_goal",
            0,
            agent.id,
            None,
            agent.goal,
            None,
            f"agent {agent.id} goal {list(agent.goal)} is unreachable on the static map",
        )
        for agent in agents
        if distance_from_goal[agent.goal][map_record.index(agent.start)] is None
    ]
    if unreachable:
        return PlanResult(
            status="unsolvable",
            method="none",
            order=(),
            paths=(),
            conflicts=tuple(sorted(unreachable, key=lambda conflict: conflict.as_key())),
            orders_tried=0,
            orders_budget=_orders_budget(len(agents), order_budget, requested_priority),
        )

    budget = _orders_budget(len(agents), order_budget, requested_priority)
    if requested_priority is not None:
        sequence: list[tuple[str, ...]] = [tuple(requested_priority)]
    else:
        sequence = _order_sequence(tuple(agent.id for agent in agents), budget)

    conflicts: list[Conflict] = []
    tried = 0
    for order_ids in sequence:
        tried += 1
        order = tuple(next(agent for agent in agents if agent.id == agent_id) for agent_id in order_ids)
        paths, failure = _run_order(map_record, order, distance_from_goal)
        if paths is None:
            if failure is not None:
                conflicts.append(failure)
            continue
        joint = detect_conflicts(order, paths)
        if joint:
            conflicts.extend(joint)
            continue
        return PlanResult(
            status="solved",
            method="priority",
            order=order_ids,
            paths=tuple(paths),
            conflicts=(),
            orders_tried=tried,
            orders_budget=budget,
        )

    if requested_priority is None:
        solution = _constraint_tree(map_record, agents, distance_from_goal, tree_budget, budget)
        if solution is not None:
            paths, tree_conflicts = solution
            if not tree_conflicts:
                return PlanResult(
                    status="solved",
                    method="constraint_tree",
                    order=tuple(agent.id for agent in agents),
                    paths=tuple(paths),
                    conflicts=(),
                    orders_tried=tried,
                    orders_budget=budget,
                )
            conflicts.extend(tree_conflicts)

    return PlanResult(
        status="unsolvable",
        method="none",
        order=(),
        paths=(),
        conflicts=tuple(_deduplicate(conflicts)),
        orders_tried=tried,
        orders_budget=budget,
    )


def _run_order(
    map_record,
    order: tuple[Agent, ...],
    distance_from_goal: dict[Point, list[int | None]],
    constraints: ConstraintSet | None = None,
    first_hold: int = 0,
) -> tuple[list[Path] | None, Conflict | None]:
    """Plan `order` one agent at a time, each treating the earlier paths as moving obstacles.

    Waiting is a legal move, but a step planner enters the grid as early as it
    can, so on a bottleneck it can walk into a pocket. Every agent is therefore
    offered a head start: it may hold its start cell for a few ticks before it
    enters the grid, and `first_hold` does the same for the highest-priority
    agent, whose early entrance can be what blocks everybody else. The first
    option that actually routes the agent is used.
    """
    constraints = constraints or {}
    planned: list[tuple[str, Path]] = []
    for index, agent in enumerate(order):
        cells, edges = constraints.get(agent.id, (frozenset(), frozenset()))
        if index == 0 and first_hold > 0:
            path, failure = space_time_astar(
                map_record,
                agent,
                planned,
                distance_from_goal[agent.goal],
                cells,
                edges,
                first_hold,
            )
            if path is None:
                assert failure is not None
                return None, failure
        else:
            path, failure = _route_with_wait(
                map_record, agent, planned, distance_from_goal, cells, edges
            )
            if path is None:
                assert failure is not None
                return None, failure
        planned.append((agent.id, path))
    return [path for _, path in planned], None


def _route_with_wait(
    map_record,
    agent: Agent,
    planned: list[tuple[str, Path]],
    distance_from_goal: dict[Point, list[int | None]],
    cells: frozenset[tuple[Point, int]],
    edges: frozenset[tuple[Point, int, Point]],
) -> tuple[Path | None, Conflict | None]:
    """Try routing `agent` after holding its start cell for 0..N ticks.

    When every option fails, a two-agent goal contention is reported as a vertex
    conflict on the shared goal: that is the concrete cause, and it is far more
    useful to a caller than the bare "no route" dead end.
    """
    failure: Conflict | None = None
    for hold in range(DEFAULT_HOLD_BUDGET + 1):
        path, conflict = space_time_astar(
            map_record, agent, planned, distance_from_goal[agent.goal], cells, edges, hold
        )
        if path is not None:
            return path, None
        if failure is None:
            failure = conflict
    assert failure is not None
    for other_id, path in planned:
        if path[-1] == agent.goal:
            return None, Conflict(
                "vertex",
                0,
                agent.id,
                other_id,
                agent.goal,
                agent.goal,
                f"agent {agent.id} cannot reach goal {list(agent.goal)}: {other_id} is "
                f"planned to end there",
            )
    for other_id, path in planned:
        if path[-1] == agent.start:
            return None, Conflict(
                "vertex",
                len(path) - 1,
                agent.id,
                other_id,
                agent.start,
                agent.goal,
                f"agent {agent.id} is trapped on {list(agent.start)}: {other_id} finishes "
                f"there at t={len(path) - 1}",
            )
    return None, failure


def _order_sequence(default_order: tuple[str, ...], budget: int) -> list[tuple[str, ...]]:
    """The deterministic priority orders to try: the default first, then permutations."""
    budget = max(1, budget)
    ordered: list[tuple[str, ...]] = [default_order]
    for permutation in sorted(permutations(default_order)):
        if len(ordered) >= budget:
            break
        if permutation != default_order:
            ordered.append(permutation)
    return ordered


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# stage two: conflict tree (outer loop of conflict-based search)
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #


def _constraint_tree(
    map_record,
    agents: tuple[Agent, ...],
    distance_from_goal: dict[Point, list[int | None]],
    tree_budget: int,
    order_budget: int = DEFAULT_ORDER_BUDGET,
) -> tuple[list[Path], list[Conflict]] | None:
    """Best-first search over sets of per-agent space-time constraints.

    Returns `(paths, [])` for a conflict-free joint plan. When no plan is found it
    returns `(infeasible_paths, [conflict])` explaining why: the failure blocking
    the best node when the tree ran out of budget, or an empty conflict list when
    every node it reached was infeasible and nothing was left to branch on.
    """
    root: ConstraintSet = {}
    paths, failure = _plan_all(map_record, agents, distance_from_goal, root, order_budget)
    if failure is None:
        return paths, []
    counter = 0
    heap: list[tuple[int, int, tuple]] = [
        (
            _paths_cost(paths) if len(paths) == len(agents) else INFEASIBLE_COST,
            counter,
            (root, paths, failure),
        )
    ]
    expanded = 0

    while heap:
        _, _, (constraints, paths, failure) = heapq.heappop(heap)
        if failure is None:
            return paths, []
        if expanded >= tree_budget:
            return paths, [failure]
        expanded += 1
        for child in _branch(constraints, failure):
            child_paths, child_failure = _plan_all(
                map_record, agents, distance_from_goal, child, order_budget
            )
            counter += 1
            heapq.heappush(
                heap,
                (
                    _paths_cost(child_paths) if child_failure is None else INFEASIBLE_COST,
                    counter,
                    (child, child_paths, child_failure),
                ),
            )
    return paths, [failure]


INFEASIBLE_COST = 1 << 40


def _plan_all(
    map_record,
    agents: tuple[Agent, ...],
    distance_from_goal: dict[Point, list[int | None]],
    constraints: ConstraintSet,
    order_budget: int = DEFAULT_ORDER_BUDGET,
) -> tuple[list[Path], Conflict | None]:
    """Plan all agents at one node of the constraint tree.

    Because a node's leaf planner plans one agent at a time, which agent yields is
    a real choice: on a bottleneck one order finds a plan and the reverse order
    traps the lower-priority agent. Every node therefore tries the deterministic
    priority orders and keeps a conflict-free plan if one appears. When none does,
    the node reports its blocking conflict so the tree can branch on it.
    """
    fallback: Conflict | None = None
    report: list[Path] | None = None
    for order_ids in _order_sequence(tuple(agent.id for agent in agents), order_budget):
        order = tuple(next(agent for agent in agents if agent.id == agent_id) for agent_id in order_ids)
        for first_hold in range(DEFAULT_HOLD_BUDGET + 1):
            outcome, failure = _run_order(
                map_record, order, distance_from_goal, constraints, first_hold
            )
            if outcome is not None:
                joint = detect_conflicts(order, outcome)
                if not joint:
                    ordered = {agent.id: path for agent, path in zip(order, outcome)}
                    return [ordered[agent.id] for agent in agents], None
                if report is None:
                    ordered = {agent.id: path for agent, path in zip(order, outcome)}
                    report = [ordered[agent.id] for agent in agents]
                conflict = joint[0]
            else:
                assert failure is not None
                conflict = failure
            if fallback is None:
                fallback = conflict
    # A plan that is complete but still conflicts names a concrete vertex or
    # swap, which is far more useful than the dead end of a single agent.
    if report is not None:
        conflicts = detect_conflicts(agents, report)
        if conflicts:
            return report, conflicts[0]
    return report or [], fallback


def _paths_cost(paths: list[Path]) -> int:
    return sum(len(path) - 1 for path in paths)


def _branch(constraints: ConstraintSet, conflict: Conflict) -> list[ConstraintSet]:
    """Children of a node: forbid the conflicted cell or edge to one of the agents.

    A two-agent conflict branches on both agents, so the tree covers "the first
    agent yields" and "the second one does". A conflict that involves a single
    agent is branched on that agent, and a bare `unreachable_goal` cannot be
    branched on at all.
    """
    if conflict.other is None:
        if conflict.type == "unreachable_goal":
            return []
        pairs = [(conflict.agent, True)]
    else:
        pairs = [
            (conflict.agent if conflict.agent < conflict.other else conflict.other, False),
            (conflict.other if conflict.agent < conflict.other else conflict.agent, False),
        ]
    children: list[ConstraintSet] = []
    for agent_id, single_agent in pairs:
        child = {key: (set(cells), set(edges)) for key, (cells, edges) in constraints.items()}
        cells, edges = child.setdefault(agent_id, (set(), set()))
        if single_agent:
            if conflict.timestep == 0:
                continue
            edges.add((conflict.position, conflict.timestep - 1, conflict.position))
        elif conflict.type == "vertex":
            cells.add((conflict.position, conflict.timestep))
        else:
            other_position = conflict.other_position or conflict.position
            edges.add((conflict.position, conflict.timestep, other_position))
            edges.add((other_position, conflict.timestep, conflict.position))
        children.append(
            {key: (frozenset(value[0]), frozenset(value[1])) for key, value in sorted(child.items())}
        )
    return children


def _deduplicate(conflicts: list[Conflict]) -> list[Conflict]:
    seen: dict[tuple, Conflict] = {}
    for conflict in conflicts:
        seen.setdefault(conflict.as_key(), conflict)
    return sorted(seen.values(), key=lambda conflict: conflict.as_key())


def _orders_budget(agent_count: int, budget: int, requested: list[str] | None) -> int:
    if requested is not None:
        return 1
    if agent_count <= 1:
        return 1
    return max(1, min(budget, _factorial(agent_count)))


def _factorial(value: int) -> int:
    total = 1
    for factor in range(2, value + 1):
        total *= factor
    return total

import unittest

from swarmgrid.model import Map, Mission
from swarmgrid.solver import (
    detect_conflicts,
    distance_map,
    makespan,
    position_at,
    space_time_astar,
)

OPEN_2X2 = {"id": "square", "width": 2, "height": 2, "grid": ["..", ".."]}


def build(map_payload, agents, mission_id="m"):
    map_record = Map.parse(map_payload)
    mission = Mission.parse({"id": mission_id, "map_id": map_payload["id"], "agents": agents}, map_record)
    return map_record, mission


class SingleAgentTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_shortest_path_avoids_obstacles(self):
        map_record, mission = build(
            {"id": "w", "width": 5, "height": 2, "grid": ["..#..", "....."]},
            [{"id": "a", "start": [0, 0], "goal": [4, 0]}],
        )
        agent = mission.agents[0]
        path, conflict = space_time_astar(map_record, agent, [], distance_map(map_record, agent.goal))
        self.assertIsNone(conflict)
        self.assertEqual((0, 0), path[0])
        self.assertEqual((4, 0), path[-1])
        self.assertEqual(6, makespan([path]))
        self.assertNotIn((2, 0), path)

    def test_waiting_is_used_when_a_cell_is_blocked_for_one_tick(self):
        map_record, mission = build(
            OPEN_2X2,
            [{"id": "a", "start": [0, 0], "goal": [1, 0]}],
        )
        agent = mission.agents[0]
        blocked = frozenset({((1, 0), 1)})
        path, conflict = space_time_astar(
            map_record, agent, [], distance_map(map_record, agent.goal), blocked
        )
        self.assertIsNone(conflict)
        self.assertEqual(((0, 0), (0, 0), (1, 0)), path)

    def test_unreachable_goal_reports_a_conflict(self):
        map_record, mission = build(
            {"id": "w", "width": 5, "height": 3, "grid": [".#...", "##...", "....."]},
            [{"id": "a", "start": [0, 0], "goal": [0, 2]}],
        )
        agent = mission.agents[0]
        path, conflict = space_time_astar(map_record, agent, [], distance_map(map_record, agent.goal))
        self.assertIsNone(path)
        self.assertEqual("unreachable_goal", conflict.type)


class OccupancyTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_a_finished_agent_no_longer_occupies_its_goal(self):
        path = ((0, 0), (1, 0), (0, 0))
        self.assertEqual((1, 0), position_at(path, 1))
        self.assertIsNone(position_at(path, 3))

    def test_following_is_legal(self):
        lead = ((0, 0), (1, 0), (2, 0))
        trail = ((1, 0), (1, 0), (1, 0), (1, 0))
        agents = (
            _agent("lead", (0, 0), (2, 0)),
            _agent("trail", (1, 0), (1, 0)),
        )
        # trail occupies (1, 0) from t=0; lead passes through it at t=1.
        # Sharing a cell is never allowed, so this plan must be reported.
        conflicts = detect_conflicts(agents, [lead, trail])
        self.assertTrue(any(conflict.type == "vertex" for conflict in conflicts))

        # When trail leaves on the same tick lead arrives, the two never share
        # the cell and the plan is clean.
        moving = ((1, 0), (1, 1), (1, 2), (2, 2))
        self.assertEqual([], detect_conflicts(agents, [lead, moving]))

    def test_a_swap_is_reported(self):
        first = ((0, 0), (1, 0))
        second = ((1, 0), (0, 0))
        agents = (_agent("a", (0, 0), (1, 0)), _agent("b", (1, 0), (0, 0)))
        conflicts = detect_conflicts(agents, [first, second])
        self.assertEqual(["edge"], [conflict.type for conflict in conflicts])
        self.assertEqual(0, conflicts[0].timestep)

    def test_sharing_a_cell_is_reported(self):
        first = ((0, 0), (1, 0), (1, 0))
        second = ((1, 0), (1, 0), (0, 0))
        agents = (_agent("a", (0, 0), (1, 0)), _agent("b", (1, 0), (0, 0)))
        conflicts = detect_conflicts(agents, [first, second])
        self.assertTrue(any(conflict.type == "vertex" for conflict in conflicts))

    def test_two_agents_settling_on_one_cell_is_a_conflict(self):
        first = ((0, 0), (1, 0))
        second = ((1, 1), (1, 0))
        agents = (_agent("a", (0, 0), (1, 0)), _agent("b", (1, 1), (1, 0)))
        conflicts = detect_conflicts(agents, [first, second])
        self.assertTrue(any(conflict.type == "vertex" for conflict in conflicts))


class JointPlanningTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_opposite_agents_in_a_corridor_are_routed_around_each_other(self):
        from swarmgrid.solver import plan_mission

        map_record, mission = build(
            {"id": "c", "width": 5, "height": 3, "grid": [".....", "..##.", "....."]},
            [
                {"id": "a", "start": [0, 0], "goal": [4, 0]},
                {"id": "b", "start": [4, 0], "goal": [0, 0]},
            ],
        )
        result = plan_mission(map_record, mission)
        self.assertEqual("solved", result.status)
        self.assertEqual([], list(result.conflicts))
        self.assertEqual(8, result.solution_makespan)
        self.assertEqual([], detect_conflicts(
            tuple(sorted(mission.agents, key=lambda agent: agent.id)), list(result.paths)
        ))

    def test_the_constraint_tree_solves_what_a_single_order_cannot(self):
        from swarmgrid.solver import _constraint_tree, plan_mission

        map_record, mission = build(
            OPEN_2X2,
            [
                {"id": "a0", "start": [0, 0], "goal": [1, 1]},
                {"id": "a1", "start": [1, 0], "goal": [0, 0]},
            ],
        )
        agents = tuple(sorted(mission.agents, key=lambda agent: agent.id))
        distances = {agent.goal: distance_map(map_record, agent.goal) for agent in agents}
        paths, conflicts = _constraint_tree(map_record, agents, distances, 64)
        self.assertEqual([], conflicts)
        self.assertEqual([], detect_conflicts(agents, paths))
        self.assertEqual(3, makespan(paths))
        self.assertEqual(((0, 0), (1, 0), (1, 1)), tuple(paths[0]))
        self.assertEqual(((1, 0), (1, 1), (0, 1), (0, 0)), tuple(paths[1]))

        priority = plan_mission(map_record, mission)
        self.assertEqual("solved", priority.status)
        self.assertEqual("priority", priority.method)
        self.assertEqual(tuple(paths), priority.paths)

    def test_the_constraint_tree_stops_at_its_node_budget(self):
        from swarmgrid.solver import _constraint_tree

        map_record, mission = build(
            {"id": "lane", "width": 4, "height": 1, "grid": ["...."]},
            [
                {"id": "a", "start": [0, 0], "goal": [3, 0]},
                {"id": "b", "start": [3, 0], "goal": [0, 0]},
            ],
        )
        agents = tuple(sorted(mission.agents, key=lambda agent: agent.id))
        distances = {agent.goal: distance_map(map_record, agent.goal) for agent in agents}
        paths, conflicts = _constraint_tree(map_record, agents, distances, 0)
        self.assertTrue(conflicts)
        self.assertEqual([], list(paths))

    def test_swapping_agents_in_a_single_lane_stay_unsolvable(self):
        from swarmgrid.solver import plan_mission

        map_record, mission = build(
            {"id": "lane", "width": 4, "height": 1, "grid": ["...."]},
            [
                {"id": "a", "start": [0, 0], "goal": [3, 0]},
                {"id": "b", "start": [3, 0], "goal": [0, 0]},
            ],
        )
        result = plan_mission(map_record, mission, tree_budget=256)
        self.assertEqual("unsolvable", result.status)
        self.assertTrue(result.conflicts)
        self.assertEqual([], list(result.paths))

    def test_a_free_map_needs_no_replanning(self):
        from swarmgrid.solver import plan_mission

        map_record, mission = build(
            {"id": "open", "width": 6, "height": 4, "grid": ["......"] * 4},
            [
                {"id": "a", "start": [0, 0], "goal": [5, 0]},
                {"id": "b", "start": [5, 3], "goal": [0, 3]},
            ],
        )
        result = plan_mission(map_record, mission)
        self.assertEqual("solved", result.status)
        self.assertEqual("priority", result.method)
        self.assertEqual(5, result.solution_makespan)


def _agent(agent_id, start, goal):
    from swarmgrid.model import Agent

    return Agent(agent_id, start, goal)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()
